name: Global Navigation
purpose: Define the persistent highest-level navigation of an Aurora application, separating global product or module destinations from product-local navigation.
problem: Without a dedicated contract, product teams or AI agents may recreate global navigation, mix global and local destinations, invent unsupported hierarchy, or treat infrastructure behavior as feature-owned behavior.

evidence.description: Global Navigation V2 with Navigation/Item Level 1 and Level 2, Default/Hover/Active/Focus/Disabled states, Navigation/Group Expanded true/false, and Navigation/Global Expanded true/false.
Application shell with Header/Hero, Navigation/Global, workspace and notification overlay.
ERP application showing Global Navigation in the shell and separate Product Navigation inside the workspace.

Explicit expand/collapse control; expanded first access; user preference persistence; independent group expansion; separation of expansion and navigation actions; active child preserves parent context; authorization controls availability; no user-configurable order in Core; keyboard accessibility requirements; future individual contracts for Navigation/Global, Navigation/Group and Navigation/Item.

Persistent Expanded, Persistent Collapsed and Temporary Expanded. Temporary expansion is triggered by pointer or focus, overlays the workspace, uses 110ms enter delay and 220ms leave/grace period; Persistent Expanded participates in layout. Structural duration is 180ms, fast duration is 120ms, easing is cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1), reduced motion preserves functionality without spatial animation, keyboard is equivalent to pointer, and touch does not depend on hover. These values were not extracted from Figma.

whenToUse: For persistent top-level navigation across the application ecosystem.
For destinations representing global products, modules or major application contexts.
whenNotToUse: For navigation inside an active product or module.
For tabs, breadcrumbs, filters, steps, transient actions, modal navigation or contextual panel navigation.
compositionRules: Global Navigation belongs to Application Shell and must not be recreated by individual features.
Global Navigation and Product Navigation must remain conceptually and structurally separate.
Level 1 represents the first supported global hierarchy.
Level 2 must belong to a documented parent group and must not exist as an orphan hierarchy level.
Do not create Level 3 or deeper hierarchy without new evidence and an explicit Aurora decision.
Expanded and Active are independent concepts: Expanded communicates visible hierarchy while Active communicates current destination.
A parent group that contains navigation children should not use the same interaction target for both navigation and expansion.
If a parent context also requires a destination page, represent that destination explicitly inside the hierarchy.
When a Level 2 item is Active, the child is the active destination while its Level 1 parent preserves contextual/expanded indication without duplicating the child's active state.
Global destination order is defined by product information architecture; user reordering is not part of the Core pattern.
Reuse approved Aurora navigation components and states.

behavior.expandCollapseControl: The explicit control chooses and persists Expanded or Collapsed. Pointer/focus may create Temporary Expanded from Persistent Collapsed without overwriting the preference.
behavior.initialState: Expanded on first access when no valid user preference exists.
behavior.preferencePersistence: Persist the authenticated user's Expanded/Collapsed preference between sessions when technically available; otherwise preserve it for the current session.
behavior.userControl: Users may keep Global Navigation collapsed as a presentation preference without changing information architecture.
behavior.groupExpansion: Navigation Groups expand and collapse independently; expanding one group does not automatically collapse another.
behavior.parentGroupAction: Expansion and destination navigation must use distinct interaction targets when both responsibilities exist.
behavior.activeHierarchy: The active Level 2 item represents the current destination. Its Level 1 ancestor preserves contextual indication but must not visually duplicate the final destination's Active state.
behavior.authorization: Authorization determines destination availability. Business permission rules remain product/system responsibilities and must not be invented by the pattern.
behavior.ordering: Global destination ordering is system/product-defined and is not user-configurable in Core v0.1.
behavior.persistentExpanded: Participates in Application Shell layout and remains expanded when pointer or focus leaves.
behavior.persistentCollapsed: Participates in layout at compact width and may expand temporarily by pointer or keyboard focus.
behavior.temporaryExpanded: Triggered from Persistent Collapsed by pointer or keyboard focus; overlays the workspace without reflow and returns after both pointer and focus leave.
behavior.pointer: Enter delay 110ms; leave/grace period 220ms; re-entry cancels pending collapse.
behavior.keyboard: Focus entry is equivalent to pointer entry; focus exit returns to Persistent Collapsed after the grace period unless pointer remains inside.
behavior.touch: Must use the explicit control and must not depend on hover.

responsive.mobile: generic Aurora navigation components include mobile variants, but Global Navigation product behavior is not-yet-validated
responsive.note: Observed component widths are not viewport breakpoints.

requirements: All destinations and controls must be operable without a mouse.
Interactive controls must expose a visible focus state.
Tab order must follow a logical navigation sequence.
Activation must follow the semantic behavior of the chosen native control.
The navigation must not create keyboard traps.
Expandable controls must expose their expanded/collapsed state semantically.
The current destination must expose its state semantically.
All interactive elements require accessible names.
Keyboard focus entering Persistent Collapsed must provide the same Temporary Expanded outcome as pointer entry.
When focus and pointer leave Temporary Expanded, return to Persistent Collapsed after the approved grace period.
Reduced motion must preserve functionality and expose the final state without spatial animation.

contentRules: Labels must represent global destinations, products, modules or major application contexts.
Do not use Global Navigation for transient actions such as Export, Save, Add or Apply Filter.
Labels and hierarchy should match the approved product information architecture.
constraints: Global Navigation must belong to Application Shell.
Product features must not recreate Global Navigation.
Do not mix global and product-local destinations.
Do not create hierarchy deeper than Level 1 -> Level 2 without explicit evidence and approval.
Do not treat Expanded as equivalent to Active.
Do not use hover as the sole or primary expand/collapse mechanism.
Do not invent responsive transformations, routing, permission logic or technical ARIA details not yet specified.
Do not expose unauthorized destinations as available navigation unless a product-specific discovery/upsell requirement explicitly defines that behavior.
Temporary Expanded must overlay the workspace; Persistent Expanded must participate in layout.
Touch interaction must not depend on hover.
antiPatterns: A feature instantiates its own Global Navigation.
Global and Product Navigation destinations appear at the same hierarchy level.
Transient actions are placed among global destinations.
Level 3 or deeper hierarchy is invented without evidence.
Expanded state is styled as if it were the active destination.
Hover-only expansion hides navigation from keyboard or touch users.
A single interaction target simultaneously navigates and expands a parent group.
Users can arbitrarily reorder the Core global information architecture.
Temporary Expanded shifts the workspace layout.
Pointer offers Temporary Expanded without keyboard-focus equivalence.
Touch requires hover to reveal navigation.

productExamples.name: ERP
productExamples.description: Global Navigation remains in the Application Shell while ERP Product Navigation operates inside the workspace.

productExamples.name: Header Notifications Open
productExamples.description: Notification overlay coexists with persistent Global Navigation and workspace.

must: Place Global Navigation inside Application Shell.
Keep Global Navigation separate from Product Navigation.
Reuse Aurora Navigation/Global, Navigation/Group and Navigation/Item structures when available.
Preserve Level 1 -> Level 2 as the deepest currently approved hierarchy.
Use Expanded as the first-access state unless a valid user preference exists.
Preserve user Expanded/Collapsed preference when the implementation supports persistence.
Keep Active and Expanded semantically distinct.
Maintain keyboard operability and visible focus.
Use Temporary Expanded from Persistent Collapsed for pointer and keyboard focus.
Overlay the workspace during Temporary Expanded and participate in layout during Persistent Expanded.
Apply Aurora v0 motion values: 110ms enter delay, 220ms leave/grace period, 180ms structural duration, 120ms fast duration and cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1).
Preserve functionality under reduced motion with instant, non-spatial state changes.
Require explicit control on touch instead of hover.
should: Prefer the shallowest supported global hierarchy.
Maintain stable global destinations across screens of the same application ecosystem.
Use product information architecture to define ordering.
Hide unavailable destinations when authorization rules say the user cannot access them, unless product requirements explicitly define another treatment.
mustNot: Recreate Global Navigation inside a feature.
Mix product-local destinations with global destinations.
Invent tablet, mobile or reduced-viewport drawer behavior.
Treat observed 380px and 56px widths as breakpoints.
Invent routing or business permission rules.
Use hover as the sole expansion mechanism.
Invent exact ARIA implementation details before accessibility/engineering validation.
Shift workspace layout during Temporary Expanded.
Provide pointer-only Temporary Expanded without keyboard-focus equivalence.

openQuestions: What exact ARIA roles, attributes and focus-restoration behavior will be standardized with Accessibility/Engineering?
What is the validated Global Navigation behavior on tablet?
What is the validated Global Navigation behavior on mobile?
Should reduced viewports use an overlay, drawer or another navigation presentation after responsive validation?

motion.provenance: Approved Aurora decision; values were not extracted from Figma.
motion.reducedMotion: Preserve interaction outcomes and final-state communication; use instant state changes without spatial animation.
motion.principle: Motion communicates transitions and is never required to understand state.
